1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

The story of Jesus fits within the larger story of the Judeo Christian tradition. The purpose of everything since creation has been to point to the life of Jesus. All of creation speaks of the majesty of God. As God created man and woman he intended them to live in peace with him forever. But because of their disobedience mankind was separated from God. But God still loved mankind so throughout the Scriptures God reveals his plan to save the world.

2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

Luke makes his introduction as the careful author of this Gospel. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. He announces to her that she has found favor with God and will give birth to Jesus, the Son of God. Through Jesus' birth, prophecies are fulfilled by the arrangement of events. God leaves no detail unnoticed. The same can be said of our own lives.

3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

One week after the baby is born, He is circumcised and officially named Jesus. While Jesus is a small boy they go to the temple where they meet a man named Simeon. The Holy Spirit had assured Simeon he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Simeon sees Jesus and declares Him the promised Messiah.

4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

John the Baptist calls out in the desert. He preaches by the river Jordan, "Turn away from your sins and be baptized, and God will forgive your sins." He is the one Isaiah predicted would make way for the Lord. The crowds gather. Immediately, he warns them not to only say they have repented. Instead, they're to follow repentance with actions that exhibit a changed heart. Jesus is baptized and receives the Holy Spirit. He kneels at the feet of someone lesser than Himself to be baptized. He demonstrates how we are to be humble.

5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

After Jesus has been baptized, He's led by the Spirit into the desert. He spends 40 days there, constantly tempted by the devil. All that time, he eats nothing. The devil tries to tempt Jesus, but Jesus answers using Scripture, resisting him.

6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

When Jesus returns to Nazareth, He goes to the synagogue. He's asked to read the Scriptures and is handed the Book of Isaiah. From it, He reads Isaiah 61:1-2. The prophecy speaks of bringing good news to the poor, proclaiming liberty to the captives, recovery of sight to the blind, freeing the oppressed, and announcing that it's time the Lord will save His people. When He finishes reading, Jesus announces to the people that the prophecy has come true as it was just read.

7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

Jesus teaches from a boat off the shore of Lake Gennesaret. He speaks in parables, giving the example of a Pharisee and tax collector going to the temple to pray. The two men approach prayer very differently. The Pharisee in the story stands by himself and lists his respectable attributes. He thanks God that he is not greedy, dishonest, or an adulterer like everyone else. He specifically points out the tax collector and thanks God for not being like him. The Pharisee boldly tells God what he does: He fasts two days a week and gives a tenth of his income. The tax collector stands at a distance from the altar. Head bowed, he beats on his chest. The only thing he prays is, "God, have pity on me, a sinner!"

8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

Jesus tells the fisherman who owns it to push out farther and let down their nets. The fisherman grumbles that he and the others have already been out all night long. They didn't catch anything. The fisherman agrees to go out and calls to his partners. Jesus sits in the boat with the fisherman. He waits expectantly. Then gathers the nets, slowly bringing something to the surface. He laughs with joy when he sees the nets are full of flopping fish. When they're done, the fisherman sits in a boat full of fish. He looks up to Jesus. The fisherman frowns and says, "Go away from me, Lord. I am a sinful man." Jesus tells him not to be afraid, that from then on, he would be a fisher of men.

9. Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life

Luke 8:41

9. Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life

Luke 8:41

Crowds press in on Jesus as He leaves the synagogue. One voice rises above the others. A man, Jairus, begs Jesus to save his sick, 12-year-old daughter. Another man runs up to Jairus. He tells him not to bother the teacher, that his daughter has died. Jesus turns and tells him not to be afraid. And that if Jairus would believe, his daughter would be well. Jesus and the disciples visit the family. The neighbors wail for the loss of the daughter. She lies lifeless on a cot. Jesus looks at her for a moment. Then He looks to the child’s mother and comforts her. He says the child isn't dead, but that she’s actually just asleep. Jesus sits and looks at the girl for a moment, then tells her to rise.

10. Disciples Chosen

Luke 5:27

10. Disciples Chosen

Luke 5:27

Jesus spots a tax collector named Matthew Levi at the gate. He collects toll money for customs as people pass through. As Jesus looks at him, Matthew senses it and looks up. Jesus says, "Follow me." Matthew watches Him go for a moment. Silently, he stands and leaves everything to follow Jesus. Later Jesus goes up a hill to pray. He prays the entire night to God. When He comes down from the hill the next morning, He gathers His followers. From them, he chooses 12 apostles. Simon (who Jesus named Peter) and Simon's brother Andrew had been the fishermen who experienced the miracle of a large catch of fish. Then Jesus chooses James and John, Philip and Bartholomew. And He chooses Matthew, the tax collector he had called at the gate. And finally Jesus chooses Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who would betray Jesus.

11. Beatitudes

Luke 6:20

Jesus looks out over the crowds gathered to hear him speak. But instead of speaking to the masses, Jesus turns back to his disciples. He encourages them for the journey ahead. He assures them that they are blessed when people hate them, reject them, insult them, and say that they are evil because they follow Jesus. He encourages them to be happy and dance for joy when that happens. Because there will be great reward in heaven for them. And He reminds them that their ancestors acted the same way toward prophets.

12. Sermon On The Mount

Luke 6:24

Jesus turns to the crowds and walks through them, teaching. He advises everyone how to walk through life in love. And talks of how, out of pride, we often judge others. He implores those who are listening to love their enemies, to actively pray for them. He speaks of offering more than what is asked of you. Do for others what you would have them do for you.

13. Blessed Are Those Who Hear And Obey

Jesus reminds us that those who hear and obey are blessed.

14. Sinful Woman Forgiven

Luke 7:36

A Pharisee invites Jesus to have dinner at His house. They're eating when a woman approaches Jesus. Everyone in the house stares, including the Pharisee. Jesus tells the Pharisee a story. He says that there were two men who owed money to someone. One owed 500 silver coins. The other owed 50. Neither men could pay their debt. So the lender canceled both debts. 15. Women Disciples

Luke 8:1

Jesus continues through the countryside. He's adamant in preaching the good news about the kingdom of God. The twelve disciples follow him. And some women follow as well. They serve the disciples, using their own resources to aid the ministry of Jesus.

16. John The Baptist In Prison

Luke 7:1

Herod has thrown John the Baptist into prison. Messengers come to him in the prison. They relay to him all that Jesus has been doing. Specifically, they tell him about a funeral procession where Jesus sees the widow who has lost her son. His heart fills with compassion. He tells the young man to get up! The son rises from the dead and goes back with his mother. After hearing this, John asks them to go ask Jesus if He's the Messiah, or if they should expect someone else. The messengers arrive where Jesus is sleeping and ask Him what John wants to know.

17. Parable Of The Sower And The Seed

Luke 8:4

The crowds press in on Jesus as He walks and teaches. He tells a parable of someone sowing seeds of grain in a field. The seed falls in a number of places, each representing something to the crowd. A disciple asks Jesus why He speaks in parables. Jesus explains the parable to the disciples. The seed that's scattered is the Word of God.

Luke 11:33

18. Parable Of The Lamp

Luke 11:33

Jesus uses a torch to explain how his followers should live. No one covers the light or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it in a place where people will see the light when they come in. He goes on to say that whatever is kept a secret will be brought into the open. And anything that's covered up will be found and brought into the light.

19. Jesus Calms The Storm

Luke 8:22

Jesus gets into a boat and tells His disciples they should all go to the other side of the lake. Along the way, Jesus falls asleep. A storm starts to rage. Waves stretch high over the bow. And the boat starts to take on water. The whole time, Jesus stays asleep. The disciples hold on tight. They try to keep the boat afloat. Finally, Peter cries out to the still sleeping Jesus. He tells Jesus that the boat is taking on water and that they'll all be drowned. Jesus stands and puts a hand out toward the storm. The storm clears. And the seas immediately calm.

20. Healing Of The Demoniac

Luke 8:26

20. Healing Of The Demoniac

Luke 8:26

Jesus and His disciples continue to sail and arrive at Gerasa. A wild man on the shore growls at their approach. Jesus hurries toward him, ahead of His disciples. The man threatens Jesus with the rock. But Jesus just continues to stare at him. The man calls Jesus by name and declares Him to be the Son of God. Jesus asks him his name. At first the man won't say. But Jesus holds out a hand to him. He says his name is Legion. He begs not to be sent back to the abyss. Instead, he wants to go into a nearby herd of pigs. Jesus puts a hand out to the pigs.

21. Jesus Feeds 5000

Luke 9:1

Jesus and the disciples continue to walk the countryside. And a great crowd follows them. Peter comes and asks Jesus to send the people away. He wants them to find food and a place to stay with local farmers and villagers. Jesus looks back out over the crowd of people. They want to hear from Jesus and have sacrificed to be there. Jesus considers this and tells the disciples to feed the people. Mary Magdalene points out that they only have a few loaves of bread and two fish. Jesus takes the baskets and proclaims to the heavens and the people, "Blessed is the Lord God, King of the Universe who brings forth bread from the earth."

22. Peter Declares Jesus To Be The Christ

22. Peter Declares Jesus To Be The Christ

Luke 9:18

Jesus asks who the crowds say He is. Peter speaks up immediately. He claims that some in the crowds say Jesus is John the Baptist. Others say He's Elijah. Others say that one of the prophets from centuries ago has come back to life. Jesus solemnly asks who Peter would say He is. Without hesitation, Peter says Jesus is God's Messiah. Jesus stares back at him.

23. The Transfiguration

23. The Transfiguration

Luke 9:28

Jesus takes John, James and Peter up a hill to pray. Jesus walks apart from them, covering His head to pray. But when He does, His appearance changes. His face changes. His clothes become pure white. He starts talking to two men who seem to be with Him. Moses and Elijah speak to Him. One says Jesus will fulfill God's purpose. The other says He will die in Jerusalem. Peter slowly wakes up. He's the first to see Moses and Elijah talking with Jesus. He wakes James and John. They see it too. Moses and Elijah turn and leave, fading away. The disciples fall to their knees and worship Jesus.

24. Jesus Heals Boy From Evil Spirit

Luke 9:37

The crowds continue to gather. They wait on Jesus. Finally, Jesus comes down the hill with Peter, James and John. One man approaches Jesus and begs that Jesus would heal his son. The boy writhes on the ground. The man goes on to say that the boy is his only son. He asked the disciples to cast out the demon. But they couldn't. Jesus gently tells the man to bring his son closer. Two men carry the boy to Jesus. But he falls again into another fit. Jesus comes to stand over him. The boy looks up. And slowly, he gets up. Now, where there were cuts and bruises on his face, there are none.

25. The Lords Prayer

26. Teaching About Prayer And Faith

Jesus has just taught them how to pray. He says, "ask and you will receive." He implores them to seek and assures that they will find. He reminds His followers that none of them would give their children bad things when they ask for good things. But the disciples should never be the cause. He looks into the crowd and says it would be better for that person to have a large stone hung around his neck and be tossed into the sea. ABOUT THIS EDITION

The Yoruba Contemporary Bible (Bibeli Mimo ni Ede Yoruba Ode-Oni) is a full Bible in modern Yoruba published by Biblica (formerly the International Bible Society), with copyright dates of 2009 and 2017. The lead translator was Dr. Ezekiel Abioye, who began the translation work in 1987; the project took approximately 30 years to complete. The translation was publicly launched on August 7, 2020, in Ibadan, Oyo State, with Prof. Iwu Ikwubuzo, Board Chairman of Biblica Nigeria, describing it as using "lucid contemporary standard variety of Yoruba Language."

John 4

Obìnrin Náà Ní Kànga

Jesu fi omi ìyè lọ obìnrin ará Samaria kan ní kànga Jakọbu, ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ará Samaria sì gbà á gbọ́. Nígbà tí ó padà sí Galili, ó fi ọ̀rọ̀ kan wo ọmọ ìjòyè ọba kan tí ó ń kú lọ sàn.

John 5

Ìwòsàn ní Adágún Bẹtisda

John 5

John 5

Ìwòsàn ní Adágún Bẹtisda

Ní ọjọ́ Ìsinmi Jesu wo ọkùnrin kan tí ó ti ṣàìsàn fún ọdún méjìdínlógójì sàn. Nígbà tí àwọn olórí kọ ọ́, Jesu kéde pé Ọmọ ni ó ń fi ìyè fúnni, ó sì ń ṣe iṣẹ́ Baba rẹ̀.

John 6

Àkàrà Ìyè

John 6

John 6

Àkàrà Ìyè

Jesu fi ìṣù àkàrà márùn-ún àti ẹja méjì bọ́ ẹgbẹ̀rún márùn-ún ènìyàn, lẹ́yìn náà ó rìn lórí òkun tọ àwọn ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀ lọ. Bí ó ti kéde ara rẹ̀ ní àkàrà ìyè, ó rí ọ̀pọ̀ tí wọ́n ń padà sẹ́yìn, ṣùgbọ́n Peteru jẹ́wọ́ pé òun nìkan ni ó ní ọ̀rọ̀ ìyè àìnípẹ̀kun.

John 7

Ní Àjọ Àgọ́

John 7

John 7

Ní Àjọ Àgọ́

Jesu gòkè lọ sí Jerusalemu ní ìkọ̀kọ̀, lẹ́yìn náà ó kọ́ni ní gbangba nínú àgbàlá tẹ́ńpìlì. Ní ọjọ́ ìkẹyìn àjọ náà ó pe àwọn tí òùngbẹ ń gbẹ láti wá sọ́dọ̀ òun mu, ìjọ ènìyàn sì pín níyà lórí ẹni tí ó jẹ́.

John 8

Ìmọ́lẹ̀ Ayé

John 8

John 8

Ìmọ́lẹ̀ Ayé

Jesu kọ̀ láti dá obìnrin kan tí wọ́n mú nínú panṣágà lẹ́bi, ó sọ fún un pé kí ó fi ìgbésí ayé ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ sílẹ̀. Ó kéde ara rẹ̀ ní ìmọ́lẹ̀ ayé, ó sì sọ fún àwọn olùfisùn rẹ̀ pé, 'Kí a tó bí Abrahamu, èmi ni.'

John 9

Ọkùnrin Tí A Bí Ní Afọ́jú

John 9

John 9

Ọkùnrin Tí A Bí Ní Afọ́jú

Jesu fi amọ̀ pa ojú ọkùnrin kan tí a bí ní afọ́jú, ó sì lọ wẹ̀ ní adágún Siloamu ó sì ríran. Àwọn Farisi wádìí rẹ̀ wọ́n sì lé e jáde, ọkùnrin náà sì sin Jesu gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ọmọ Ènìyàn.

John 10

Olùṣọ́-àgùntàn Rere

John 10

John 10

Olùṣọ́-àgùntàn Rere

Jesu ni olùṣọ́-àgùntàn rere tí ó fi ẹ̀mí rẹ̀ lélẹ̀ fún àwọn àgùntàn, àwọn àgùntàn rẹ̀ sì mọ ohùn rẹ̀. Ní Àjọ Ìyàsímímọ́ ó kéde pé, 'Èmi àti Baba jẹ́ ọ̀kan,' àwọn olórí sì gbìyànjú láti mú un.

John 11

Àjíǹde Lasaru

John 11

John 11

Àjíǹde Lasaru

Jesu sọkún ní ibojì ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ̀ Lasaru, lẹ́yìn náà ó pè é jáde kúrò nínú ibojì lẹ́yìn ọjọ́ mẹ́rin. Iṣẹ́ àmì náà mú kí ọ̀pọ̀ gbàgbọ́, ìgbìmọ̀ sì pinnu pé Jesu gbọ́dọ̀ kú.

John 12

Wákàtí Náà Ti Dé

John 12

John 12

Wákàtí Náà Ti Dé

Maria fi òróró pa ẹsẹ̀ Jesu ní Betani, ó sì wọ Jerusalemu pẹ̀lú igbe 'Hosana.' Jesu kéde pé wákàtí náà ti dé fún Ọmọ Ènìyàn láti gba ògo, bí hóró àlìkámà tí ó bọ́ sí ilẹ̀ tí ó sì kú.

John 13

Wíwẹ Ẹsẹ̀ Àwọn Ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn

John 13

John 13

Wíwẹ Ẹsẹ̀ Àwọn Ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn

Ní oúnjẹ alẹ́ ìkẹyìn Jesu wẹ ẹsẹ̀ àwọn ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀, ó sì sọ fún wọn pé kí wọ́n ṣe bí òun ti ṣe. Ó sọ àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ ìdàlẹ̀bi Judasi àti ìsẹ́ Peteru, ó sì fún wọn ní òfin tuntun: kí ẹ fẹ́ràn ara yín.

John 14

Ọ̀nà, Òtítọ́ àti Ìyè

John 14

John 14

Ọ̀nà, Òtítọ́ àti Ìyè

Jesu tu àwọn ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀ nínú: ó ń lọ pèsè ààyè sílẹ̀ ní ilé Baba rẹ̀, òun tìkára rẹ̀ sì ni ọ̀nà tọ Baba lọ. Ó ṣe ìlérí Ẹ̀mí Mímọ́, ó sì fi àlàáfíà rẹ̀ sílẹ̀ fún wọn.

John 15

Àjàrà àti Àwọn Ẹ̀ka

John 15

John 15

Àjàrà àti Àwọn Ẹ̀ka

Jesu ni àjàrà tòótọ́, àwọn ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀ sì ni àwọn ẹ̀ka, tí a pè láti wà nínú rẹ̀ kí wọ́n sì so èso. Ó pàṣẹ fún wọn pé kí wọ́n fẹ́ràn ara wọn, ó sì kìlọ̀ pé ayé yóò kórìíra wọn bí ó ti kórìíra òun.

John 16

Iṣẹ́ Ẹ̀mí

John 16

John 16

Iṣẹ́ Ẹ̀mí

Jesu ṣe ìlérí Ẹ̀mí òtítọ́, tí yóò dá ayé lẹ́bi tí yóò sì tọ́ àwọn ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn sínú gbogbo òtítọ́. Ìbànújẹ́ wọn yóò di ayọ̀: 'Ẹ tújúká! Èmi ti ṣẹ́gun ayé.'

John 17

Jesu Gbàdúrà fún Àwọn Ọmọlẹ́yìn Rẹ̀

John 17

John 17

Jesu Gbàdúrà fún Àwọn Ọmọlẹ́yìn Rẹ̀

Jesu gbé ojú rẹ̀ sókè ọ̀run ó sì gbàdúrà fún ara rẹ̀, fún àwọn ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀, àti fún gbogbo àwọn tí yóò gbàgbọ́ nípasẹ̀ ìhìn wọn. Ó bèèrè pé kí wọ́n lè jẹ́ ọ̀kan, bí òun àti Baba ti jẹ́ ọ̀kan.

John 18

Ìdàlẹ̀bi àti Ìmúni

John 18

John 18

Ìdàlẹ̀bi àti Ìmúni

Judasi mú àwọn ọmọ ogun lọ sí ọgbà náà, wọ́n sì mú Jesu wọ́n sì gbé e lọ síwájú Annasi, Kaiafa, àti Pilatu. Peteru sẹ́ ẹ ní ẹ̀ẹ̀mẹta, àkùkọ sì kọ.

John 19

Ìkànmọ́ Àgbélébùú

John 19

John 19

Ìkànmọ́ Àgbélébùú

Pilatu fi Jesu lé wọn lọ́wọ́ láti nà án àti láti kàn án mọ́ àgbélébùú ní Gọlgọta, lábẹ́ àkọlé tí ó kà pé 'Ọba àwọn Júù.' Jesu fi ìyá rẹ̀ lé Jòhánù lọ́wọ́, ó kéde pé 'Ó parí,' wọ́n sì sin ín sínú ibojì kan nínú ọgbà.

John 20

Ibojì Òfìfo

John 20

John 20

Ibojì Òfìfo

Maria Magdalene rí i pé a ti yí òkúta náà kúrò, ó sì pàdé Jesu àjíǹde nínú ọgbà náà. Jesu farahàn àwọn ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀ lẹ́yìn ìlẹ̀kùn tí a tì, Tomasi olùṣiyèméjì sì jẹ́wọ́ pé, 'Olúwa mi àti Ọlọ́run mi!'

John 21

Oúnjẹ Àárọ̀ Ní Etí Òkun

John 21

John 21

Oúnjẹ Àárọ̀ Ní Etí Òkun

Jesu àjíǹde pàdé àwọn ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn méje tí wọ́n ń pẹja ní Òkun Galili, ó sì fi ẹja púpọ̀ kún àwọ̀n wọn. Lórí oúnjẹ àárọ̀ ní etí òkun ó dá Peteru padà, ó bi í ní ẹ̀ẹ̀mẹta pé, 'Ǹjẹ́ o fẹ́ràn mi?' ó sì pàṣẹ fún un pé, 'Bọ́ àwọn àgùntàn mi.'

Luke 1

Àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ Ìbí Méjì

Luke 1

Luke 1

Àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ Ìbí Méjì

Angẹli Gabrieli kéde ìbí Jòhánù Onítẹ̀bọmi tí ń bọ̀ fún Sakariah àti ti Jesu fún wúndíá Maria. Maria kọ orin ìyìn sí Ọlọ́run, wọ́n sì bí Jòhánù fún Elisabeti ní ògbólógbòó ọjọ́ orí rẹ̀.

Luke 2

Ìbí Jesu

Luke 2

Luke 2

Ìbí Jesu

A bí Jesu ní Bẹtilẹhẹmu a sì tẹ́ ẹ sínú ibùjẹ ẹran, àwọn angẹli sì kéde ìhìn náà fún àwọn olùṣọ́-àgùntàn. A mú un wá sí tẹ́ńpìlì, ní ọmọ ọdún méjìlá ó sì ya àwọn olùkọ́ lẹ́nu ní ilé Baba rẹ̀.

Luke 3

Iṣẹ́ Òjíṣẹ́ Jòhánù Onítẹ̀bọmi

Luke 3

Luke 3

Iṣẹ́ Òjíṣẹ́ Jòhánù Onítẹ̀bọmi

Jòhánù wàásù ìtẹ̀bọmi ìrònúpìwàdà ní odò Jordani, ó sì tọ́ka sí ẹni tí ó tóbi jù tí ń bọ̀. A tẹ Jesu bọmi, Ẹ̀mí sọ̀kalẹ̀ bí àdàbà, a sì tọpasẹ̀ ìlà ìdílé rẹ̀ padà títí dé Adamu.

Luke 4

Ìdánwò àti Ìkọ̀sílẹ̀ ní Nasareti

Luke 4

Luke 4

Ìdánwò àti Ìkọ̀sílẹ̀ ní Nasareti

Jesu gbààwẹ̀ fún ogójì ọjọ́ ní aginjù, ó sì ṣẹ́gun àwọn ìdánwò Èṣù pẹ̀lú Ìwé Mímọ́. Nínú sínágọ́gù Nasareti ó kéde pé ìlérí Isaiah ti ṣẹ, ìlú rẹ̀ tìkára rẹ̀ sì lé e jáde.

Luke 5

Pípe Àwọn Ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn Àkọ́kọ́

Luke 5

Luke 5

Pípe Àwọn Ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn Àkọ́kọ́

Lẹ́yìn ìkó ẹja ìyanu, Peteru, Jakọbu, àti Jòhánù fi ọkọ̀ wọn sílẹ̀ láti tẹ̀lé Jesu. Jesu wẹ adẹ́tẹ̀ kan mọ́, ó dárí jì ó sì wo ọkùnrin arọ kan sàn, ó sì pe Lefi agbowó-orí.

Luke 6

Olúwa Ọjọ́ Ìsinmi

Luke 6

Luke 6

Olúwa Ọjọ́ Ìsinmi

Jesu kéde pé Ọmọ Ènìyàn ni Olúwa ọjọ́ Ìsinmi, ó sì yan àwọn àpọ́sítélì méjìlá. Ní pẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ kan ó bùkún àwọn tálákà, ó pàṣẹ ìfẹ́ sí àwọn ọ̀tá, ó sì sọ ìtàn àwọn ọ̀mọ̀lé méjì — ọ̀kan lórí àpáta, ọ̀kan lórí iyanrìn.

Luke 7

Ìgbàgbọ́ Balógun Ọ̀rún

Luke 7

Luke 7

Ìgbàgbọ́ Balógun Ọ̀rún

Jesu ṣe ìyanu sí ìgbàgbọ́ balógun ọ̀rún ará Romu kan, ó sì jí ọmọkùnrin kan ṣoṣo opó kan dìde ní Naini. Ó dá ìbéèrè Jòhánù Onítẹ̀bọmi láti inú ẹ̀wọ̀n lóhùn, obìnrin ẹlẹ́ṣẹ̀ kan sì fi omijé rẹ̀ wẹ ẹsẹ̀ rẹ̀.

Luke 8

Òwe Afúnrúgbìn

Luke 8

Luke 8

Òwe Afúnrúgbìn

Jesu sọ òwe afúnrúgbìn ó sì fi ọ̀rọ̀ kan mú ìjì rọlẹ̀. Ó tú ọkùnrin kan tí ẹgbẹ́ ọmọ ogun ẹ̀mí èṣù ń bá gbé sílẹ̀, ó wo obìnrin kan tí ẹ̀jẹ̀ ń ṣàn lára rẹ̀ sàn, ó sì jí ọmọbìnrin Jairu dìde.

Luke 9

Bíbọ́ Ẹgbẹ̀rún Márùn-ún

Luke 9

Luke 9

Bíbọ́ Ẹgbẹ̀rún Márùn-ún

Jesu rán àwọn Méjìlá jáde, ó bọ́ ẹgbẹ̀rún márùn-ún ènìyàn, Peteru sì jẹ́wọ́ rẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí Mesaya Ọlọ́run. Lórí òkè Jesu pàrọ̀ dà nínú ògo, lẹ́yìn náà ó kọ ojú rẹ̀ sí Jerusalemu.

Luke 10

Ará Samaria Rere

Luke 10

Luke 10

Ará Samaria Rere

Jesu rán àwọn ońṣẹ́ àádọ́rin-ó-lé-méjì ṣáájú rẹ̀, ó sì yọ̀ nítorí ìfihàn Baba fún àwọn ọmọ kékeré. Ó dá ìbéèrè 'Ta ni aládùúgbò mi?' lóhùn pẹ̀lú òwe ará Samaria rere, Maria sì yan ìpín tí ó dára jù lábẹ́ ẹsẹ̀ rẹ̀.

Luke 11

Ìkọ́ni Nípa Àdúrà

Luke 11

Luke 11

Ìkọ́ni Nípa Àdúrà

Jesu kọ́ àwọn ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀ láti gbàdúrà pé, 'Baba, kí orúkọ rẹ di mímọ́.' Ó ń lé àwọn ẹ̀mí èṣù jáde pẹ̀lú ìka Ọlọ́run, ó sì kéde ègbé sí àwọn Farisi tí wọ́n ń fọ òde ago.

Luke 12

Ẹ Má Bẹ̀rù, Ẹ̀yin Agbo Kékeré

Luke 12

Luke 12

Ẹ Má Bẹ̀rù, Ẹ̀yin Agbo Kékeré

Jesu kìlọ̀ nípa àgàbàgebè àti ojúkòkòrò, ó sì sọ ìtàn ọlọ́rọ̀ aṣiwèrè kan tí ẹ̀mí rẹ̀ parí ní alẹ́ tí àká rẹ̀ kún. Ó pe àwọn ọmọlẹ́yìn rẹ̀ láti gbẹ́kẹ̀lé Baba tí ń bọ́ àwọn ẹyẹ ìwò, àti láti wà ní ìmúrasílẹ̀ fún wíwá Ọmọ Ènìyàn.

Luke 13

Ẹnu-ọ̀nà Tóóró

Luke 13

Luke 13

Ẹnu-ọ̀nà Tóóró

Jesu pe gbogbo ènìyàn láti ronúpìwàdà, ó wo obìnrin abirùn kan sàn ní ọjọ́ Ìsinmi, ó sì fi ìjọba wé hóró músítádì. Ó rọ̀ wọ́n láti wọlé gba ẹnu-ọ̀nà tóóró, ó sì sọkún lórí Jerusalemu, ìlú tí ń pa àwọn wòlíì.

Luke 14

Àsè Ńlá

Luke 14

Luke 14

Àsè Ńlá

Ní tábìlì Farisi kan Jesu kọ́ àwọn àlejò láti gba ipò ìsàlẹ̀ àti àwọn onílé láti pe àwọn tálákà. Ó sọ ìtàn àsè ńlá kan tí àwọn àlejò tí a pè kọ̀ láti wá, ó sì pe àwọn ọmọ-ẹ̀yìn láti ka iye owó rẹ̀.

Luke 15

Àgùntàn, Owó, àti Ọmọ Tí Ó Sọnù

Luke 15

Luke 15

Àgùntàn, Owó, àti Ọmọ Tí Ó Sọnù

Fún àwọn Farisi tí ń kùn Jesu sọ ìtàn olùṣọ́-àgùntàn tí ó fi àgùntàn mọ́kàndínlọ́gọ́rùn-ún sílẹ̀ láti wá ọ̀kan, àti ti obìnrin tí ń wá owó rẹ̀ tí ó sọnù. Baba kan sáré láti gbá ọmọ rẹ̀ onínàákúnàá tí ó padà mọ́ra: 'Ó ti sọnù, a sì ti rí i.'

Luke 16

Ọlọ́rọ̀ àti Lasaru

Luke 16

Luke 16

Ọlọ́rọ̀ àti Lasaru

Jesu sọ ìtàn ìríjú ọlọ́gbọ́n kan ó sì kọ́ni pé kò sí ẹni tí ó lè sin Ọlọ́run àti owó pọ̀. Ọlọ́rọ̀ kan kọ ojú sí Lasaru alágbe ní ẹnu-ọ̀nà rẹ̀, ó sì rí i pé ipò wọn ti yí padà ní ìkọjá ibojì.

Luke 17

Mẹ́wàá Tí A Wò Sàn Nínú Ẹ̀tẹ̀

Luke 17

Luke 17

Mẹ́wàá Tí A Wò Sàn Nínú Ẹ̀tẹ̀

Jesu wo adẹ́tẹ̀ mẹ́wàá sàn, ọ̀kan ṣoṣo — ará Samaria — ni ó padà wá dúpẹ́. Ó kọ́ni pé ìjọba Ọlọ́run wà láàrin wọn, ó sì sọ nípa ọjọ́ tí a ó fi Ọmọ Ènìyàn hàn.

Luke 18

Opó Aláìṣàárẹ̀

Luke 18

Luke 18

Opó Aláìṣàárẹ̀

Jesu sọ ìtàn opó kan tí ìforítì rẹ̀ mú ìdájọ́ òdodo wá, àti ti agbowó-orí kan tí a gbọ́ àdúrà ìrẹ̀lẹ̀ rẹ̀ ju ti Farisi kan lọ. Ó gba àwọn ọmọ kékeré, ó tako ìjòyè ọlọ́rọ̀ kan, ó sì fi ìríran fún alágbe afọ́jú kan nítòsí Jeriko.

Luke 19

Sakeu Agbowó-orí

Luke 19

Luke 19

Sakeu Agbowó-orí

Jesu pe Sakeu sọ̀kalẹ̀ láti orí igi sikamórè, ìgbàlà sì dé ilé rẹ̀. Ó wọ Jerusalemu pẹ̀lú igbe ìyìn, ó sọkún lórí ìlú náà, ó sì wẹ tẹ́ńpìlì mọ́.

Luke 20

Àwọn Ìbéèrè Nípa Àṣẹ

Luke 20

Luke 20

Àwọn Ìbéèrè Nípa Àṣẹ

Àwọn olórí tako àṣẹ Jesu, ó sì fi òwe àwọn agbẹ̀ búburú dáhùn. Ó yí ìdẹkùn wọn nípa owó orí Kesari àti nípa àjíǹde padà sí wọn.

Luke 21

Àwọn Àmì Òpin

Luke 21

Genesis 22

Wíwo Ìgbàgbọ́ Ábrámù

Chapter 7

Genesis 37

Chapter 8

Chapter 8

Genesis 39

Jósẹ́fù àti Aya Pótífárì

Ní Íjíbítì, Jósẹ́fù gòkè dé ipò ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé nínú ilé Pótífárì. Lẹ́yìn tí ó kọ̀ ìfẹ́ aya Pótífárì, a fi ẹ̀sùn èké kàn án a sì jù ú sínú ẹ̀wọ̀n — síbẹ̀ Olúwa wà pẹ̀lú rẹ̀.

Lẹ́yìn ìran púpọ̀, fáráò titun dìde tí kò rántí Jósẹ́fù. Àwọn Hébérù pọ̀ sí, a sì fi ipá mú wọn sínú ìsìnrú kíkorò. Láàárín wọn, a fi ọmọkùnrin Hébérù kan tí orúkọ rẹ̀ ń jẹ́ Mósè pamọ́ sínú ọmọ-igbó, ó sì dàgbà nínú ààfin fáráò.

Mósè àti Igbó tí Ń Jó

Lẹ́yìn tí ó sá kúrò ní Íjíbítì, Mósè ń tọ́jú agbo ní Mídíánì. Ní Òkè Hórébù, Olúwa fara hàn nínú igbó kan tí ń jó láìjórẹ́, ó sì rán Mósè padà sí Íjíbítì láti mú àwọn ènìyàn rẹ̀ jáde nínú ìsìnrú.

Mósè dojúkọ fáráò, àwọn ìyọnu bọ́ sí Íjíbítì, a sì pa ọ̀dọ́-àgùntàn Ìrékọjá. Ísírẹ́lì gba òmìnira ó sì gba Òkun Pupa kọjá lórí ilẹ̀ gbígbẹ. "Iwe adura Bibeli Mimọ" of 1879 is a volume of Yoruba prayers with selections from the Psalms and other Scripture portions, issued by the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge for use in the Anglican congregations of Abeokuta, Ibadan, Lagos, and the Sierra Leone diaspora. The Yoruba Scripture behind this edition is the work of Samuel Ajayi Crowther (c. 1809-1891) and the team of repatriated Saro translators and catechists associated with the Church Missionary Society mission to Yorubaland.

Crowther, born in Osogun in the Oyo Empire, had been enslaved as a boy in 1821, liberated by a Royal Navy anti-slavery patrol, and educated at Fourah Bay in Sierra Leone. He joined the 1841 Niger Expedition, was ordained in London in 1843, and became the first African Anglican bishop in 1864. His Yoruba translation of the Gospels appeared from the late 1840s, the New Testament was completed in 1862, and the full Yoruba Bible was published by the BFBS in 1884 after decades of revision. The 1879 Psalms and liturgical portions stand in the stream of that work.

The translation set Yoruba orthography for the following century, establishing the system of subdots and tonal accent marks that remains in use. Yoruba Scripture circulates today among tens of millions of speakers across southwestern Nigeria, Benin, Togo, and the African diaspora in Brazil and the Caribbean.

he 1887 Yoruba New Testament, titled Testamenti Titun ti Jesu Kristi Oluwa ati Olugbala Wa (The New Testament of Jesus Christ Our Lord and Saviour), is a British and Foreign Bible Society reissue of the translation first completed by Samuel Ajayi Crowther (c. 1809-1891) and his Church Missionary Society collaborators. Crowther had been taken from his Yoruba village of Osogun as a child in 1821 by slave raiders, freed by a British anti-slavery squadron in 1822, and settled at Freetown, Sierra Leone, where he was baptized in 1825.

Crowther learned Latin, Greek, and Hebrew at the CMS Fourah Bay Institution, and was ordained deacon in 1843 and priest in 1845. He returned to Yorubaland as part of the CMS Niger Expedition, establishing the Abeokuta mission in 1846. In 1864 he was consecrated at Canterbury as the first African Anglican bishop, responsible for the CMS Niger Mission.

The Yoruba Bible translation proceeded in portions from the 1840s onward. Crowther issued Matthew in 1850 and the complete New Testament in 1862, working with Thomas King, James White, and CMS colleagues at Abeokuta and Ibadan. The Old Testament was completed in 1884. Crowther also compiled a Yoruba grammar and dictionary (1843, 1852), the first scholarly study of the language.

The 1887 New Testament revision incorporated orthographic adjustments proposed by the CMS Yoruba Revision Committee and circulated as Crowther's career entered its final, contested decade. Crowther's Niger Mission came under sustained attack in the later 1880s from younger European CMS missionaries who accused his African clergy of laxity, a campaign that reshaped African Anglican leadership at the close of his life.

Lamin Sanneh treats Crowther's Yoruba Bible as foundational for modern African Christianity, the first major Scripture translation in a West African language led by an African bishop (Sanneh 2009).
